prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker for everyone — the right one depends on what coverage you want (ACA individual plan, short‑term, HSA‑eligible, dental/vision, or small‑group if you have employees), whether you want ongoing service or a one‑time enrollment, and whether you prefer a local agent vs. an online broker. That said, here’s a practical way to find the best broker for a self‑employed person in Kansas City, MO — plus some reputable options and what to ask when you interview them.

How to find a good broker
- Use HealthCare.gov’s “Find Local Help” (or Missouri’s insurance department site) to locate licensed, certified navigators and brokers who can assist with Marketplace/ACA enrollments.  
- Choose an independent broker/agency that represents multiple carriers (not a captive agent who only sells one company).  
- Prefer licensed agents who specialize in individual/sole‑proprietor policies and have recent experience with ACA enrollments and premium tax credits/subsidies.  
- Check reviews on Google/Yelp and confirm licensing with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance (or Kansas if you live on the KS side of the metro).

Reputable broker platforms and resources to consider
- HealthCare.gov / Find Local Help — for certified navigators and brokers who can enroll you in Marketplace plans and check eligibility for subsidies (free).  
- HealthSherpa — a widely used, ACA‑friendly online broker that integrates with HealthCare.gov and makes comparing subsidy‑eligible plans easy.  
- eHealth and PolicyGenius — larger online broker/comparison services that show many plan options (good for fast comparisons).  
- Local independent insurance agencies — often provide more hands‑on, year‑round service (find via HealthCare.gov or Missouri insurance department).

What to ask a broker (short checklist)
- Are you licensed in Missouri (and Kansas, if needed)?  
- Do you specialize in individual/sole‑proprietor clients? How many do you serve?  
- Which carriers do you represent? Are you independent or captive to one insurer?  
- Do you help with Marketplace (HealthCare.gov) enrollments and premium tax credit calculations?  
- What are your fees (do you charge a client fee or are you paid by carrier commissions)?  
- Will you provide year‑round support (billing, claims appeals, renewals)?  
- Can you explain HSA‑eligible plans, deductibles, networks, and out‑of‑pocket maxes for my situation?

Other tips specific to self‑employed people
- Always check whether you qualify for premium tax credits on the ACA Marketplace — they can dramatically reduce cost.  
- If you want pre‑tax savings, look for HSA‑eligible high‑deductible plans.  
- If you have contractors/employees, ask about small‑group options or using a PEO/association plan.  
- Consider brokers who can help with 1095 forms and tax implications of health insurance for self‑employed.

If you’d like, tell me:
- your Kansas City zip code,  
- whether you want ACA-compliant plans (Marketplace), short‑term, HSA, or small‑group options, and  
- whether you prefer a local agent vs. an online service —

…and I’ll look up a few licensed brokers/agents or navigator resources in your exact area and recommend the best next steps.
